doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Racial interaction in jazz and 'Crow Jim'
summary: He discusses reverse racism, says playing settles disputes, and doubts claims that the 1950s scene was harmonious.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well I’m glad you brought that up because I’ve been curious about the racial interaction in jazz and if it’s changed over the years.

I think there was always some kind of a racial problem. I mean obviously from the black end there was definitely a big problem. From the white end of it, we used to refer to it as “Crow Jim” you know, reverse racism. Whereas if you were white you really didn’t have a right to play this music. And some white musicians actually gave up music, I mean actually believe that. And my belief is, you know it sounds cliché, but I mean it doesn’t matter what color you are, if you can play you can play. So I used to say, “Okay, we can’t play? I can’t play? Come on up on the bandstand — let’s see who can play and let’s see who can’t play.” You know you can talk all night long but put your money where your mouth is. And that usually settled most of the problems. But on the other hand, it still does exist today, on both ends, and I think it’s a problem we’re going to have for eternity. I mean we’ve got to learn to live with it. And the other thing is we can’t take it as seriously as most people — you know it’s like if somebody says this little thing, it’s politically incorrect, and I mean it’s to the point now where it’s ridiculous. And I think that’s half the problem. Let’s not take it — let’s try to relax and just try to get along, and

the next thing you know it will happen, you know? If you listen to some of the white musicians from the ‘50s they say that, you know, they got along fine with everybody. Well maybe from their end it looked that way, but maybe it wasn’t. Who knows? I wasn’t really on the scene at that level then so I can’t really comment on it but I’ve heard it from both ends. And everybody said everything was cool. But I don’t know, I wonder.
